prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical proposal and the first experimental demonstrations of strong coupling between a single microwave photon and a superconducting artificial atom, establishing circuit quantum electrodynamics and dispersive readout

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B024) to circuit QED (B016). The deciding point is that my round-1 reason for hesitating over B016, closeness to the 2025 prize, was answered on the physics. Johansson, Mehlig and Pearce showed that the 2025 work established quantum behaviour of a macroscopic circuit variable (tunnelling and level quantisation), whereas circuit QED is coherent exchange between one photon in a resonator and an engineered atom, with dispersive readout and the bus architecture that follow from it. These are different results. I can judge the underlying many-body and light-matter physics only from the outside, but the achievement is concrete, dated 2004, replicated for twenty years, and the credit fits the three-name limit as theory (Blais) plus two experimental groups (Wallraff, Schoelkopf). Mehlig's proposal to keep the citation to strong coupling and dispersive readout makes the trio defensible. The chair's summary also shows B016 and B031 as the only configurations with three explicit supporters each, and B016 is the one that every member ranked.
statement.case_against: Girvin and Huang co-authored the founding proposal and Yale was larger than Schoelkopf, so any trio leaves out people with real claims, and a narrow citation only partly cures that. The 2025 adjacency is reduced but not removed, and I still hear the point that this is an enabling architecture rather than a finding about nature. Johansson's and Lindroth's proximity to the field and to Wallraff's institution has to be handled openly if B016 advances. Against my former choice, the round-1 exchange did not dislodge my view that the flat-band prediction and the correlated states are real and reproduced, but it did establish that the experimental credit without Yuan Cao and the Dean, Young and Kim groups is contestable, and that the pairing mechanism is a further, if secondary, reason to wait.

responses.point: Mehlig argued that the first author of the 2018 experiments, Yuan Cao, is not credited, so the experimental attribution of B024 is weaker than that of circuit QED, and that the mechanism should be better understood first; he would keep the B016 citation to strong coupling and dispersive readout.
responses.response: I accept the attribution point and no longer think I can defend B024 as ready this year. I still maintain that the existence of the correlated phases is not in doubt, so I treat the mechanism as a secondary issue and Cao and the parallel moire groups as the primary one. I adopt your narrow citation for B016: it is what keeps the trio defensible, and it leaves the transmon and later error-correction work, and with them Devoret and Girvin, to another discussion.

responses.point: Johansson separated circuit QED from the 2025 prize by calling it coherent single-photon exchange with an engineered atom, with dispersive readout and a bus architecture, and acknowledged that his Chalmers centre may warrant discounting his support.
responses.response: That technical distinction is what moved me, and your disclosure is the right one. I would not discount your scientific argument, since it was specific and checkable, but I would ask that the committee not count your first place as independent support, and that the final tally be read with that in mind. Even without it, Mehlig, Pearce and now I reach B016 on the merits. I also agree with you that B031 is the best fallback, and I list it as an alternative.

responses.point: Pearce moved circuit QED to first after reading the round-1 ballots, said the 2025 adjacency is a risk to be managed and not a merit, and thought moire matter should wait for the mechanism and the credit boundary to settle.
responses.response: I agree that following a recent award is a risk, not an argument, and I do not use it in favour. On your reading of B024 I think you are right on credit and partly right on maturity, so I concede the substance while keeping the view that it is a strong candidate for a later cycle. Your request that the citation rest on light-matter coupling and not on the earlier tunnelling work is one I share, and I have worded mine accordingly.

responses.point: Kroll prefers the optical lattice clock (B031) with Katori and Ye as the cleanest two-name credit, reproduced near 1e-18, and argued that the 2005 and 2012 prizes do not contain the magic-wavelength many-atom idea.
responses.response: Your lineage answer is persuasive: the magic-wavelength condition is a distinct physical idea and not a comb refinement. I cannot judge priority within metrology, so I take Lindroth's caveat on Lemonde, Lisdat and the ion-clock groups seriously, and I rank B031 as my second alternative rather than lower. I still place B016 ahead, because the committee would be signalling one new area at the moment when its Girvin and Huang question is smaller than the ion-clock and lattice-priority question you yourself raise. If B016 were to fail on conflict or recusal grounds, I would support B031 without hesitation.

responses.point: Lindroth ranked B031 first as the case where discovery, attribution and maturity leave the fewest open questions, and flagged a possible recusal question for B016 because of her collaboration with Keller's group at ETH, Wallraff's institution.
responses.response: I respect that the clock case is the cleaner one on attribution, and your disclosure about ETH is appropriate. I would not regard a collaboration with a different group at the same institution as a serious conflict, and I would hope you vote on the merits, but that is for you and the chair to decide. My difference with you is small and mainly about how to weigh the three-name credit: Girvin and Huang are an unresolved point, but the proposal and both strong-coupling experiments are unambiguous, whereas the early lattice-clock demonstrations came from several groups at about the same time.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts circuit QED as distinct from the 2025 macroscopic-tunnelling prize, and whether the citation can be worded so that this is evident.
Whether the exclusion of Girvin, Huang and the wider Yale group survives a closer check of the 2004 history than I can make as a non-specialist.
How disclosed proximities (Johansson at Chalmers, Lindroth at ETH-linked groups) should affect the weight given to B016 support.
Whether B031 is ready now or should wait for the redefinition of the second; I cannot judge metrological priority.
Whether B024 should be revisited in a later cycle once the pairing mechanism and the credit for Cao and the parallel groups are clearer.
statement.conflict_note: My profile documents no personal or institutional tie to Blais, Wallraff or Schoelkopf, nor to any other credited name. My own field, electronic-structure theory and correlated electrons, is adjacent to B024 and B043, which I previously favoured, and I note that I have now moved away from my own field-adjacent choice. I have no declared conflict with B016.
